first.rationale: The two observed declines are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), which points at the funnel-friction candidates (memory_86, memory_31, memory_91) rather than at the competitor's pricing move. Promotional pricing is the tempting response to the competitor, but memory_73 explicitly records that it bought acquisition/revenue at the cost of 30-day retention and warns against generalizing it; under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that caveat should be honored, not overridden by competitive urgency. Referral incentives (memory_57) address established customers, not the failing top-of-funnel; enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to the SMB-side declines. I spend the verification budget on the two live competitors for the slot: memory_86 (shortened onboarding) because it is my intended action and I need the original record's effect size, segment, and whether the lift was on completion alone or carried through to retained revenue; and memory_91 (activation messaging) because if its week-one engagement lift actually translated into durable first-value rather than just clicks, it may dominate onboarding for this slot. I did not re-verify memory_31 since it overlaps memory_86's mechanism. Downstream value risk: memory_31's lever was cutting required signup fields, which can strip qualification data and degrade the sales-assisted enterprise path (memory_44) and lead quality — the shortened flow must not be applied to enterprise-intent traffic, and the experiment should measure retained/qualified revenue, not completion rate alone. Uncertainty preserved: these memories are consolidated summaries from days 12-61, the competitor entry is a new regime, and the declines could be composition effects (losing price-sensitive SMBs) rather than friction; so this runs as a standard experiment with a holdout and a retention-and-qualified-revenue readout, and I will revise toward activation_messaging if the archive shows memory_86's lift was completion-only.

final.rationale: Both archive pulls came back confirmed, and they resolved the question I spent the budget on: memory_86's onboarding lift was not completion-only vanity — completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and crucially 30-day retention +3%, i.e. the gain persisted past the point where promotional pricing (memory_73) leaked it back. Activation messaging (exp_91) is also real but weaker on the durable axis (+6% activation, +1% retention). Onboarding therefore dominates on the primary objective, and it sits upstream: onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, and a shortened flow feeds the activation step, so this single slot plausibly addresses both declines while activation messaging addresses only the second. I am holding the line against promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing being the loudest signal this week: memory_73 records acquisition and revenue lift purchased with a material 30-day retention loss and an explicit instruction not to generalize it, which is precisely the trade that fails a sustainable-qualified-revenue objective. Referral incentive targets established accounts, not the leaking top of funnel; enterprise_sales_assist is orthogonal to the SMB-side declines. Implementation constraint from the downstream-value risk I flagged earlier: I will use memory_86's mechanism (shorten and resequence the onboarding steps) rather than memory_31's mechanism of stripping required signup fields, because removing qualification fields can degrade lead quality and undercut the demo-request path that memory_44 shows outperforms self-serve for enterprise pipeline; enterprise-intent traffic is excluded from the shortened flow. Uncertainty that survives verification: exp_86 ran pre-competitor-entry, so part of the current decline may be segment composition (losing price-sensitive SMBs outright) rather than friction, in which case onboarding repair will underperform its historical effect size. Hence a standard experiment with a holdout, read out on retained and qualified revenue plus downstream lead quality — not on completion rate — rather than a broad rollout on the strength of a day-52 record.
